narrative.overview:
This is a monochrome field with one voice in it. The neutral scale does all the structural work — surfaces, borders, reading text, dividers — and a single saturated teal appears only where attention has actually been earned: one word per section heading, the icons that label a fact, the counters, the primary action. The palette is neutral by decision, not by timidity. Colour here is a signal, and a signal that fires everywhere is noise.

The character is precise and engineered. Spacing is regular rather than expressive, states are predictable, every interactive element has a real focus ring, and nothing is placed by feel. The audience for this system is engineers reading it as a work sample, so a misaligned edge reads exactly like a bug in the code — the discipline is the argument. It is also alive without being busy: sections reveal once on scroll, the hero counters run once and stop, two borders trace slowly enough to read as highlights rather than as animation. Motion is authored in single moments; nothing loops fast enough to pull the eye off the text.

Dark is the native environment, not an option. defaultTheme="dark", and the teal was chosen for how it reads on graphite. The light theme is fully correct and fully supported, but it is the translation, not the original.
keyCharacteristics: One saturated accent against a strictly neutral scale; a coral sibling used five times in the whole page
Dark-first, with the light theme derived rather than designed twice
Tonal layering carries structure; a three-step shadow scale carries only state and layer
Softly rounded geometry (10px base radius), pill shapes reserved for labels and filters
Single type family; hierarchy comes from size and weight alone
Motion is slow, one-shot, and fully removable under prefers-reduced-motion

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Teal at full chroma clears contrast only against dark backgrounds. It is for display-size type, icons, and fills — never body copy, never small links. Reading text is text-foreground / text-muted-foreground; teal-toned text is text-accent-foreground. text-primary-alt is under the same restriction and stricter still (2.62:1 on the light background): display or decorative only.

rules.name: The Token Law
rules.body: A colour that is not a token does not exist. No hex, no rgb(), no arbitrary Tailwind value (bg-[#1b1828]), no inline style={{ color }}. A new colour means a variable in :root — and in .dark unless it is deliberately theme-constant — plus an @theme inline entry, added in src/styles/globals.css and nowhere else. Opacity modifiers on tokens (bg-primary/10, bg-muted/30) are the sanctioned way to get a lighter reading of an existing colour.

rules.name: The One Palette Rule
rules.body: A component installed from a registry that ships its own :root/.dark block has that block stripped on install. There is exactly one palette in this project.

rules.name: The Literal Class Rule
rules.body: Tailwind 4 compiles only class names it can read as literal text in the source. A class assembled at runtime — a template literal such as text-[${item.color}], or 'text-' + tone — produces no CSS at all, silently: the code type-checks, lints, and renders with no colour. Per-item colours therefore live in the data as complete token class names (tint: 'text-brand-telegram') and reach the element through cn().

rules.name: The Single Accent Word Rule
rules.body: Every section heading carries exactly one teal word — Frontend Developer, Featured Projects, Let's Connect. Not a gradient, not the whole line, not two words. The heading is where the signal is spent.

rules.name: The No Second Voice Rule
rules.body: No second font family, no uppercase tracked eyebrow above sections, no monospace as a texture. If something needs to feel different, it changes weight or size.

rules.name: The No Horizontal Scroll Rule
rules.body: 360px is the floor, and nothing may overflow it. Test the real copy at 360 / 768 / 1280 before calling a layout done.

rules.name: The Structure-Is-Tonal Rule
rules.body: Structure is tone plus a hairline: if a surface needs to read as separate, change its tone and give it a 1px border. Ambient seats a surface or a control on the page — that is its whole job, and it is why every filled and outlined control carries it at rest. What a shadow may never do is rank things: it does not replace tonal structure, and it does not mark one element as more important than its neighbour. Depth above ambient is earned only by a state change (raised) or by floating above the page (overlay).

rules.name: The Three Steps Rule
rules.body: Ambient, raised, overlay. Do not use Tailwind's stock shadow-xs…shadow-2xl in this project; they are theme-blind and invisible on graphite. A fourth step means a token, not a one-off shadow-[...].

rules.name: The No Halo Rule
rules.body: Every shadow carries a vertical offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset coloured glow is decoration, and the hero's blurred teal orbs already own that register.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: 1px, all four sides, border-border. No coloured border-left accent bars, no 2px emphasis borders, no border as decoration. Three exceptions are exhaustive: a thicker border is legitimate only as a focus ring, as a frame around a photograph (the avatar), or as a background-coloured knockout (the timeline dot). Wanting something to look more important is not a fourth reason.

rules.name: The Pill Means Label Rule
rules.body: A pill is a badge, a chip, or a filter. An action is a md-radius rectangle. Do not round a button to a pill to make it look friendlier.

dos: Do add every new colour, radius, or shadow as a token in src/styles/globals.css — variable in :root (and .dark unless theme-constant) plus an @theme inline entry — and then run npm run design:sync so DESIGN.md's frontmatter and .impeccable/design.json follow. There is no Tailwind config file; that stylesheet is the only place values live.
Do spend the teal on one thing per region: one accent word, one primary action, one set of icons.
Do use text-accent-foreground for teal-toned text and links; reserve text-primary for display-size type, icons, and fills.
Do separate sections by alternating bg-background and bg-muted/30, and keep every section on py-12 inside mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8.
Do give every interactive element the standard focus ring (focus-visible:ring-[3px] ring-ring/50 with focus-visible:border-ring).
Do gate every non-essential animation behind prefers-reduced-motion — motion-reduce:animate-none, a motion-safe: prefix, useReducedMotion(), or simply not rendering the effect.
Do check both themes and 360 / 768 / 1280 with the real copy before calling any change done.
donts: Don't write a raw colour anywhere: no #FE8FB5, no bg-[#1b1828], no text-[#a3cfff], no inline style={{ color }}. This has happened twice already — the contact form's shine stops, and the messenger icons before Telegram Blue and WhatsApp Green became tokens.
Don't build a class name at runtime to get a per-item colour. It compiles to nothing — see The Literal Class Rule.
Don't use Tailwind's stock shadow-xs…shadow-2xl. They are theme-blind and vanish on graphite — use shadow-ambient / shadow-raised / shadow-overlay.
Don't put text-primary or text-primary-alt on body copy, small links, or captions. They fail contrast on the light background.

Don't reintroduce hand-written utility classes of the .gradient-text / .glass-effect / .button-primary / .container-custom / .card-hover kind. Containers are mx-auto max-w-7xl, buttons are Button variants, panels are Card.
Don't add gradient text, a second font family, a tracked uppercase eyebrow over sections, or monospace used as a "technical" texture.
Don't hand-write a primitive the shadcn registry ships, and don't paste registry source by hand — install it and reconcile it with these tokens and the repo's conventions.
Don't add a coloured border-left accent bar, or a border above 1px for emphasis. Thicker strokes exist in exactly three sanctioned places (focus ring, avatar frame, timeline knockout) — see Shapes.
Don't use depth to rank elements. Ambient is uniform across surfaces and controls; if something needs to read as more important, that is colour, size, or position — not a bigger shadow.
Don't nest a card inside a card, or let a grid of identical icon-heading-text cards become a section's whole structure.

Don't spread --destructive into decoration. It means failure, and --primary-alt is the decorative sibling. The hero beam's leading stop is the single sanctioned exception (see Components); do not cite it to justify a second one.
Don't revive the --chart-* or --sidebar-* tokens as a shortcut to a new colour. Nothing under src/ reads them today, and they are excluded from this document on purpose.
